criterion: ROADMAP proposal P6 (dated proposals of 2026-10-21): split radiance cascades for diffuse GI, toward M5 criterion 1. Target from the table: raw-hall diffuse indirect at 1080p on the RTX 4090 under 6 ms; relative RMSE against the 8-bounce path trace at least 30% below lighting model 2's 0.43; a thin-wall leak scene included. Kill: the leak scene's RMSE exceeds the no-GI baseline.
written: 2026-10-22, before any code and before any run
source: Freeman, Sannikov and Pitt-Francis, 'Split Radiance Cascades: Real-Time Global Illumination via Sparse Radiance Probes' (arXiv 2607.20384, 2026). Only the abstract could be read (the PDF exceeded the fetch limit): world-space probes in a sparse hash map, rays traced from visible surfaces, each ray's contribution assigned to cascade intervals by its hit distance (ray splitting). Everything below beyond those three ideas, and the cascade merge of Sannikov's original radiance cascades, is this engine's own design, written fresh; nothing is copied.

baseline.model_2: raw-hall nave 512 x 320, pt-error 128 spp 8 bounces: relative RMSE 0.432895, bias -0.317057, noise floor 0.0766 (evidence/m3-lighting-v2-runs.json l5; reproduced locally on 2026-10-22 at 5206cf7 with the same digits)

design.lighting_model_3: radiance = albedo x (0.2 x sky + li max(0, n.l) x sun + I). sky and sun are lighting model 2's (computeRTVisibility, unchanged). I is the diffuse indirect term: the cosine-weighted mean, over the receiver's hemisphere, of the radiance arriving from surfaces (rays that escape carry 0 here, because the sky is already in model 2). Model 2 is untouched; model 3 exists only in the new gi command.
design.bounce_cache: A world-space cache of irradiance E (rgb, model-3 units: the bracket above) keyed by (cell, normal bucket): cells of 0.25 m over the scene box padded by 0.5 m, buckets the six signed dominant axes of the normal, stored densely over the box. Every frame each receiver ray's first hit h1 makes one estimate at h1: one sun shadow ray, and one cosine ray from h1 whose radiance is 0.2 on escape or albedo(h2) x E(h2) from the previous frame's cache on a hit. The estimate is added in fixed point (1/4096) into h1's entry; after the frame each entry with samples blends its frame mean in with weight max(1/(f+1), 1/8). Multiple bounces come from the recursion through the cache, one more bounce a frame.
design.receiver_rays: From every receiver pixel (stride 1 for the error runs; one ray per 2 x 2 block at 1080p for the timing) one cosine ray a frame, seeded by pixel and frame, from p + 1e-3 n. Its radiance is albedo(h1) x E(h1) after this frame's cache update, or 0 on escape.
design.ray_splitting: Four cascades. Cascade c has probes on cells of 0.25 x 2^c m keyed by (cell, normal bucket of the receiver), octahedral direction bins of (8 x 2^c)^2 over the sphere, and the hit-distance interval [r_c, r_c+1) with r = 0, 0.5, 2, 8, infinity m. A ray with hit distance t (infinity on escape) counts as entering interval c when t >= r_c, and as hitting in it when r_c <= t < r_c+1, adding its radiance there. For each cascade the probe is the cell of the ray's origin and the bin is the ray direction at that cascade's resolution. Counts and radiance sums are u32 in fixed point (1/4096), so the sums do not depend on thread order.
design.sparse_probes: A probe exists where a receiver lands: per cascade a dense occupancy mark over (cell, bucket) from the G-buffer, an exclusive prefix sum gives each occupied key a slot in key order (deterministic, the same on the CPU and the GPU), and only slots carry bin data. The hash map of the paper becomes this mark-and-scan table, because the WGSL subset the translator accepts has no compare-exchange.
design.merge: From the coarsest cascade down: R_c(slot, bin) = S_c / n_c + (1 - h_c / n_c) x R_c+1, with S_c the radiance sum, h_c the hits and n_c the entries of that bin; R_c+1 is the mean of the four child bins at cascade c+1, interpolated trilinearly over the eight c+1 probes of the same bucket around the c probe's cell centre, weights renormalised over the probes that exist (the parent cell always exists). A bin with no entries passes R_c+1 through. Beyond the last interval R = 0.
design.gather: Each cascade-0 probe's merged bins are projected onto real spherical harmonics up to l = 2 (bins weighted by their octahedral solid angle, from 4 x 4 sub-directions a bin). A receiver's I is the clamped-cosine convolution of the SH (Ramamoorthi and Hanrahan 2001) at its normal, divided by pi, from the eight cascade-0 probes around it, trilinear, renormalised over occupied ones.
design.reference: The CPU reference runs the same algorithm with geometry queries through the engine's PLOC tree (raw/renderer/rt_bvh.hpp, float32, the arithmetic the GPU's traversal repeats) and everything after the hit (estimates, cache blend, merge, SH, gather) in float64. Ray directions are generated in float32 the same way on both sides.
design.gpu: One WGSL module (src/renderer/gpu/shaders/gi.wgsl) translated to HLSL for D3D12 and SPIR-V like every pass; it consumes the CPU G-buffer and model 2 visibility, so its parity measures the GI passes alone.
design.run: raw_native_cli gi --owned-scene NAME --width W --height H [--gpu] [--frames 40 --warmup 8] --out DIR writes frame_hdr.pfm (model 3) and mask.pgm for pt-error, indirect.pfm, and gi.json (parameters, hashes, parity and timings).

scenes.raw-hall-nave: the owned hall, its camera, 512 x 320 for error, 1920 x 1080 for time
scenes.leak-room: new owned scene, generated in code: a closed room 12 x 4 x 6 m of 0.2 m walls, split at x = 0 by a 2 cm wall (thin against every cell size here) with a 1 m doorway at its far end; a 2 x 2 m skylight over the west half admits the sun; the camera stands in the east (dark) half looking at the thin wall and the doorway
scenes.control-sphere: the convex sphere alone: no ray from it can hit anything

g1_unchanged.what: every existing output: the model 2 frame of raw-hall (frame_hdr.pfm hash above), the identity and golden jobs
g1_unchanged.bound: byte-identical; the gi command is new and lighting models 1 and 2 are not touched

g3_hall_error.what: raw-hall nave 512 x 320, model 3 from the CPU reference (40 frames, 8 warm-up), pt-error 128 spp 8 bounces
g3_hall_error.prediction: 0.22 to 0.32, low confidence. Model 2's own error against 1 bounce is 0.286 (l4, mostly its 64-ray sky noise and an unexplained structured residue); relative to the 8-bounce mean that alone is about 0.19 to 0.2, so even a perfect indirect term leaves a floor near 0.2. Bias should move from -0.317 to within +-0.1.

g4_leak.what: leak-room 512 x 320, model 3 against model 2, both through pt-error 128 spp 8 bounces
g4_leak.bound: model 3's relative RMSE below model 2's (the kill criterion)
g4_leak.prediction: holds, moderate confidence; the leak to watch is the coarse cascades (1 and 2 m cells) straddling the thin wall in directions the fine intervals leave open. Recorded beside it: the mean of I on east-half floor pixels within 0.5 m of the wall against the path tracer's indirect there (pt 8 bounces minus pt 1 bounce).

g5_gpu_parity.what: I and the model 3 frame from the GPU against the CPU reference, raw-hall 256 x 160 and leak-room 256 x 160, 12 frames (4 warm-up), on WARP and lavapipe in CI and on the RTX 4090
g5_gpu_parity.bound: relative RMSE of I over covered pixels at most 2e-3; model 3 frame relative RMSE at most 1e-3. Float32 hits may flip at triangle edges against the CPU's float64 shading of the same hits, which these bounds allow and a broken pass does not

g5c_control.what: RAW_NATIVE_GI_CONTROL=nomerge (test-only): the GPU merge ignores occlusion (h treated as 0)
g5c_control.prediction: fails by far: far-field light comes through every wall

g6_cpu_golden.what: tests/test_gi_cascades.cpp: leak-room 128 x 80, 6 frames, the SHA-256 of I as float32
g6_cpu_golden.bound: one hash per compiler family (MSVC, GCC), pinned from the first green CI run; every later drift gets a dated note
g6_cpu_golden.prediction: MSVC and GCC may differ (float64 libm); thread count must not change the hash

g7_time.what: raw-hall nave at 1920 x 1080 on the RTX 4090 through the shared GPU lock: one steady-state frame of every GI pass (rays, cache, splitting, merge, SH, gather), the dispatch-timer method of evidence/gpu-dispatch-timer-bounds.json (median of 21 submit-to-fence times)
g7_time.prediction: 3 to 7 ms, low confidence: about 1.5 M rays a frame through a 250,000-triangle tree in compute, plus the merge over about 50 M bins

does_not_prove: Specular or glossy indirect (the term is diffuse only); a moving camera or moving geometry (probes accumulate over a static view; history decay is not built); scenes larger than a dense cache over their box allows; that the paper's own scheme behaves the same (only its abstract was read); GPU time without submission latency.
